items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 32:1
items.html: (To the question) In the permission of the groom, which is the upper Aba and Ima, her Mochin are equal to the Mochin of ZA, for ZA receives there the aspect of the Mochin of Aba, and the Nukva receives there the Mochin of Ima; and their statures are found equal. But in the house of the Nukva, she receives the Mochin in the manner of the degree, namely from the coupling made in the head of ZA, and she does not have the root of the Gevurot themselves, namely the male Gevurot that come from the first restriction, but only the aspect of the Gevurot of the Malchut of Ima, which is the aspect of the second restriction — except that she receives an illumination from the crown of Gevura of ZA, which is the aspect of the root of the Gevurot. And since now she needs the illumination of the Gevurot of ZA, and she is an offshoot of his Mochin, therefore both of them do not use a single Keter.
